content: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany criticizes UEFA’s Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, arguing they protect established clubs rather than fostering competition. Kompany believes FFP hinders newer or smaller clubs from competing against well-established teams financially, citing Manchester City's success under Sheikh Mansour's ownership as an example of how significant investments can lead to a club's growth and community benefits. He contends that FFP rules prevent emerging teams from challenging the traditional elite, thus maintaining the status quo.

England Sevens international Jeff Williams has signed with Bath for the upcoming season, bringing with him valuable experience from the World Series circuit where he has scored 36 tries. Bath's head coach, Mike Ford, sees Williams as a dynamic addition who will fit well with their attacking style, while England Sevens head coach Simon Amor praised Williams' physical play and development as a player. Williams, born in South Africa but with an English father, previously played for clubs in Cape Town and France before his move to Bath.

Director David Ayer revealed the first full look at Jared Leto portraying the Joker in "Suicide Squad," a film set to be released in 2016 without the presence of Batman. Leto has transformed for the role by cutting his hair and shaving his face, stepping into the shoes of Heath Ledger as the iconic comic book villain. The film, which also features Will Smith, Margot Robbie, and other actors, will hit theaters on August 5, 2016.

Three Florida corrections officers, including a former trainee, have been charged with plotting to murder a former inmate, according to the Florida Attorney General's office. They allegedly joined an undercover branch of the KKK and conspired to kill the inmate, who they had previously fought with. The FBI staged a fake crime scene to convince the suspects their plan had succeeded, and all three face up to 30 years in prison if convicted.

The conference call for Manny Pacquiao regarding his upcoming fight with Floyd Mayweather was abruptly cancelled due to technical difficulties, affecting over 10-15 years of successful calls with the same service provider. Pacquiao managed to answer only one question during the brief call, stating his training was "very good." The call was rescheduled due to the large number of participants, with Mayweather set to hold his own call the following day.

Serena Williams received a large cake to celebrate her 700th career victory at the Miami Open, following her victory over Sabine Lisicki. Meanwhile, Andy Murray also celebrated his 500th win with a cake presentation. Williams advanced to the semi-finals but missed a chance to play her sister Venus, who lost in the earlier rounds.

Beijing International Airport is constructing the world's largest terminal, Terminal 1, to accommodate a significant rise in Chinese tourists traveling internationally. Designed by Zaha Hadid, this six-tier terminal will span 700,000 square meters and cater to 45 million passengers annually, aiming to enhance connectivity and reduce walking distances through a spacious, pillar-less design featuring a central multi-layered courtyard. The terminal reflects China's growing global presence, with outbound tourism increasing from 10 million in 2000 to 109 million in 2014, contributing $164 billion to the economy.

Manchester United's manager, Louis van Gaal, reported that Wayne Rooney suffered a knee injury during Manchester United's 3-0 loss to Everton, though the severity is still unknown. This setback follows back-to-back league defeats under Van Gaal’s management, which has now allowed Liverpool to close the gap in the race for Champions League qualification. The injury occurred in the closing stages of the match, with Rooney being substituted and seen receiving treatment.

Manchester City is reportedly considering signing Jack Wilshere, who was recently seen showing off his extensive shopping trip on Instagram. During his day off, the Arsenal midfielder shared photos of his grocery haul, which included various cereals, eggs, baked beans, and corn on the cob, aimed at aiding his recovery from ankle surgery. Wilshere humorously sought help from his followers to assist with unloading his heavily stocked trolley.

A Venezuelan woman named Marleni Olivo threw a mango inscribed with her contact information at President Nicolas Maduro during a rally, an act that gained widespread attention and went viral. In response, Maduro offered Olivo an apartment through the country's housing program, praising her boldness. While some criticized the incident, Maduro used it to highlight his housing initiatives and praised Olivo's initiative.

Carlos Tevez, a former Manchester United and City striker, believes it is more challenging to score goals in Serie A compared to the Premier League. He attributes this to the higher defensive presence and less dynamic midfield play in Italian football, despite having scored 36 goals in Serie A since joining Juventus in 2013. Tevez also suggests that his current Juventus team is more balanced and harder to beat than the teams he played with during his time at Manchester United.

Jamie Carragher criticized Yaya Toure for allegedly ducking out of the way during a free-kick taken by Jason Puncheon, which secured Crystal Palace's victory over Manchester City. This incident, which occurred during a Premier League match at Selhurst Park, was seen as particularly unacceptable given the size of the wall formed by City players. The criticism highlighted Toure's perceived lack of commitment compared to his teammates in defending against the goal.

A 50-year-old Australian man died in Kuta, Bali, after collapsing at a hotel restaurant and reportedly suffering a heart attack. The incident occurred at the Rooftop Restaurant of the 101 Legian Hotel where the man was staying with a friend. Police and the Australian Consulate are investigating the circumstances and considering whether to conduct an autopsy to determine the exact cause of death.

Former Australian cricket captain and commentator Richie Benaud was honored with a private funeral service in Sydney, attended by close family, friends, and former teammates, after declining a state funeral offer from the Australian Prime Minister. Benaud, known for both his playing career and extensive commentary work, passed away at the age of 84 due to skin cancer complications. The event, marked by a memorial booklet titled "Remembering Richie," underscored Benaud's significant impact on cricket both as a player and commentator, beloved by fans worldwide.

Isobel Attwood, a 16-year-old schoolgirl from Winchester, Hampshire, has been missing for two days and is believed to be with a man in his 20s in Southampton, according to friends who posted on social media. Police are concerned for her welfare and believe she could be in the Winchester or Southampton areas, though they have not yet been able to locate her despite several leads. Authorities are urging anyone with information to contact them.

If Manchester City fail to qualify for the Champions League this season, key players like Sergio Aguero, David Silva, Joe Hart, and Yaya Touré could lose out on £500,000 each in bonuses due to incentivized contracts tied to European qualification. The club faces a crucial period, with matches against West Ham, Aston Villa, Tottenham, Queens Park Rangers, Swansea, and Southampton, as they seek to secure their top-four finish and avoid missing out on the lucrative Champions League. Manchester United's victory over Manchester City has put pressure on City to improve their performance and remain competitive in the race for European spots.

Martin Skrtel, a Liverpool defender, has dismissed rumors linking him with moves to Wolfsburg or Napoli, stating he plans to remain with Liverpool despite his contract expiring in 2016. His agent has confirmed that Skrtel is in the process of finalizing a new contract with the club and that no offers from other clubs are currently on the table. Despite Liverpool's poor season, the team is expected to undergo changes in the summer, but Skrtel appears committed to staying with the Premier League side.

Cheryl Rios, a female CEO from Texas, sparked controversy by claiming that women should not be president due to their "hormones," which she believes would prevent them from starting wars. Her comments were met with widespread criticism and accusations of misogyny, particularly on social media. Despite defending her right to express her opinions, Rios maintained that she supports women in other professions while reiterating her belief that they are unsuitable for the presidency.

Mario Mandzukic, despite suffering injuries in a physical Champions League match against Real Madrid, is expected to be fit for the return leg at the Bernabeu. Atletico Madrid coach Diego Simeone believes Mandzukic will recover in time for the game, while also indicating that another attacking option, Antoine Griezmann, is in good form and likely to feature. The second leg is set for Wednesday, with Simeone confident about his team's prospects.

Chelsea's Jose Mourinho prepared his team to face Marouane Fellaini, only to learn from a hotel doorman that the Manchester United player was not going to play due to being there to get tickets for Eden Hazard. This confusion led Mourinho to discover that it was actually Fellaini's twin brother, Mansour, who had posed for pictures at the hotel. Despite the misunderstanding, Fellaini did play in the match at Stamford Bridge, which Chelsea won 1-0, moving closer to securing the Premier League title.

Dawn Milosky, a 45-year-old woman from Beachwood, New Jersey, was involved in a serious accident where her 2006 Toyota Solara convertible overturned and caught fire. Police responding to a tip about erratic driving rescued Milosky, who had been knocked unconscious, just as the car began to burn; she required emergency medical attention including defibrillation and CPR. Milosky has been charged with driving while intoxicated, reckless driving, and other related offenses.

A farmer in eastern China has found himself in the spotlight after one of his goats gave birth to a six-legged kid, dubbed a "spider goat" by Chinese internet users. The baby goat, born 20 days ago, initially had four forelegs and two hind legs but as it grew, two of the forelegs became shorter and cannot touch the ground. The farmer, Xiao Qibin, plans to let the unusual goat grow naturally without attempting to remove the extra legs.

West Ham United is considering signing Javier Hernández from Real Madrid as part of their summer recruitment plan. The 26-year-old striker, known as "Little Pea," is set to return to Manchester United at the end of the season and could be available for around £7 million. Alongside this, West Ham is also targeting young players such as Pedro Obiang, Moussa Konate, and Fabian Schar.

Stuart McCall, the manager of Rangers, has dismissed the notion that his future with the club will be decided before the end of the season, emphasizing that the team's recent success has not yet translated into significant achievements. Despite leading the team to three consecutive victories and restoring a positive atmosphere at the club, McCall insists that no meaningful discussions with the board regarding his contract will occur until after the play-offs. Additionally, the article mentions that Shane Ferguson, who was previously involved in a controversial loan deal with Newcastle United, is expected to join Rangers next week, though McCall is cautious about Ferguson's immediate contribution due to a long-term knee injury.

Werder Bremen secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Hamburg SV in a crucial match, thanks to an 84th-minute penalty by Franco Di Santo, which kept Bremen's hopes of a Europa League spot alive. Despite new coach Bruno Labbadia's losing return to Hamburg's bench, the match resulted in a significant defeat for the club, leaving them at the bottom of the table. Meanwhile, second-placed Wolfsburg aims to close the gap on league leaders Bayern Munich in their upcoming match against Schalke 04.

A two-year-old boy fell into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after slipping between a 10 to 12-foot gap while being held by his parents, who managed to rescue him before emergency services arrived. The child suffered minor injuries and was listed in stable condition after being taken to the hospital, though the zoo plans to press child endangerment charges against the parents. The zoo has also closed the exhibit pending an investigation.

Russian TV channel TV Rain gave Hillary Clinton's campaign video a mature audience rating due to concerns it might violate Russia's anti-gay propaganda law, which bans the promotion of non-traditional sexual relationships to minors. The video featured a brief scene of a gay couple holding hands, leading the channel to mark it as 18+ to avoid potential legal issues. This decision reflects the uncertainty surrounding the interpretation of the law and the channel's cautious approach to avoid scrutiny from authorities.

Siem de Jong, a Newcastle United player who recently returned from a collapsed lung, made a 45-minute appearance for the Under 21s team, coming off the bench at halftime during their 2-0 loss to Derby County. Despite the encouraging return, de Jong's performance was somewhat underwhelming, suggesting that he may not be ready for the upcoming match against Tottenham. Additionally, Facundo Ferreyra, another Newcastle player on loan, substituted for de Jong at halftime but has yet to make a senior appearance due to persistent injuries.

Chef Ally Lees from Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a massive omelette for Easter that measures three feet in circumference and contains 12,000 calories and 945g of protein, far exceeding the recommended daily intake. The dish, made with 150 eggs, required an hour to cook using a large paella pan and would take at least five people to finish. Ally, despite having tasted it himself, admitted he couldn't consume the entire omelette due to its excessive protein content.

Three Olympic gold medalists from the 2012 London Games—Jessica Ennis-Hill, Mo Farah, and Greg Rutherford—will participate in the Sainsbury’s Anniversary Games at the Olympic Stadium. The event, which features a two-day Diamond League meeting and the IPC Athletics Grand Prix Final, is set to take place from July 24-26 and aims to recreate the excitement of the 2013 edition. Ticket sales have begun, with prices ranging from £10 to £20 for adults.

In a shocking discovery, police in Rio de Janeiro found that a popular snack bar was using the meat of stray dogs to make pastries, specifically pastels, a traditional Brazilian dish. The owner, a Chinese national named Van Ruilonc, admitted to using the dogs, which he claimed were strays, for the fillings. This revelation came alongside an investigation into allegations of forced labor and slave-like conditions among Chinese workers employed at the business.

Ebony Dickens, a resident of East Point, Georgia, posted a threatening message on Facebook under a fake name, calling for black people to kill white police officers, which led to her arrest by local and federal law enforcement agencies. The post, which detailed plans to kill multiple white cops, garnered significant attention and prompted a thorough investigation. Upon identifying Dickens, authorities found a firearm and several computers at her home during a subsequent search warrant.

PSV Eindhoven won the Dutch Eredivisie championship for the first time in seven seasons by defeating Heerenveen 4-1, securing 79 points and leaving second-place Ajax behind. Key contributors included Luuk de Jong with two headed goals and Memphis Depay with a stunning free kick. Meanwhile, bottom team Dordrecht faced a challenging situation, moving closer to relegation with a 3-0 loss to Vitesse Arnhem.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva was reportedly beaten to death by his head teacher, Lalit Verma, at Dwarika Prasad School in Railamau village, India, after being accused of stealing a pencil and eraser. The severe beating led to Shiva's death upon arrival at the hospital due to internal bleeding. This incident has sparked further investigations and legal action against Verma, who has admitted to slapping Shiva during questioning.

A gastrointestinal illness affecting 100 passengers and five crew members has been reported on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship, out of a total of 2,117 passengers and 964 crew members. The Centers for Disease Control is investigating the cause, while the ship is currently in San Diego after recent stops in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico. This is the third such outbreak on the Celebrity Infinity, with previous incidents occurring in 2006 and 2013.

A Boston Terrier named Gizmo, filmed by its owner Loren Mathieson, was seen performing an unusual walking technique after trying on new booties. In the footage, Gizmo appears to stand on its front paws and lift its hind legs to walk in a vertical position before reaching his owner. The amusing video, capturing Gizmo's acrobatic movements, has garnered over 80,000 views and left viewers amused.

New Orleans has implemented a city-wide smoking ban, which took effect on Wednesday, prohibiting smoking in most indoor public places such as bars, casinos, and restaurants. Despite initial concerns from bar owners about potential revenue loss and objections from some smokers, the ban was passed unanimously by the city council in January. The ban is part of an effort to protect workers' health and comes just before major events like Mardi Gras and jazz festivals.

Manchester United secured a hard-fought victory against West Ham United in the Under 21 Premier League, moving four points clear at the top of the table. West Ham took an early lead through Reece Oxford's header, but Manchester United quickly responded with goals from Josh Harrop and Joe Rothwell, with Adnan Januzaj leading the team as captain. Despite Jordan Brown equalizing just before halftime, Manchester United held on to win, thanks to Harrop's second goal from a mix-up in the West Ham goal.

The Anglican Archbishop of Brisbane, Phillip Aspinall, has joined a call to abolish Queensland's 'gay panic' defense, which can reduce murder charges to manslaughter under certain circumstances. Aspinall expressed support for the removal of this defense and appealed against violence, including incidents at anti-Islam rallies and church vandalism, emphasizing the need to overcome fear with constructive responses. During an Easter Sunday mass, Aspinall also encouraged his congregation to find hope and resilience in the spirit of resurrection.

Sandra Bullock has been named the world's most beautiful woman by People magazine for 2015, marking her as the oldest recipient of the honor in its history. In a candid interview, Bullock downplays the accolade, emphasizing the importance of being kind, content, and authentic rather than focusing on physical appearance. The cover story also highlights Bullock’s family life and her approach to aging gracefully.

An improvised bomb explosion near a U.N. vehicle in Garowe, northeastern Somalia, killed six people, including four UNICEF aid workers, according to the United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia. The attack, claimed by Al-Shabaab, follows another ambush that killed three African Union troops in the Lower Shabelle region on Sunday. Somalia's President denounced the attack as an assault on the nation's future and strongly condemned it.

Gary Saurage, the manager of Gator Country wildlife park in Beaumont, Texas, was called to capture a 400-pound, 11-foot-long alligator from a family's backyard pond using only his hands. The alligator, which proved particularly aggressive, was successfully removed and taken to the park. The incident highlights the need for residents to maintain proper barriers against alligators and emphasizes Saurage's point that alligators are not a threat if kept at a safe distance.

In recent clashes in eastern Turkey, five members of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) were killed and one wounded, while four Turkish soldiers were injured. In response, Turkish Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan condemned the violence. This incident follows calls from jailed PKK leader Abdullah Ocalan for an end to the conflict and a move towards peace talks.

Two 18-month-old twin boys tragically died after accidentally falling into a canal in Yuma, Arizona. The boys were found in the water over two hours after they disappeared, and despite rescue efforts, they were pronounced dead at the hospital. A family member was reportedly nearby during the incident, and investigators do not suspect foul play.

Orlando City, a Major League Soccer team coached by Adrian Heath, has shown interest in acquiring Javier Hernández from Manchester United, potentially capitalizing on his popularity among Latin American fans. Meanwhile, several European clubs, including eight from the Premier League and others like Wolfsburg, AC Milan, and Lazio, are also interested in Hernández, who has struggled during his loan at Real Madrid. Additionally, Manchester United has offered a revised contract to young midfielder Andreas Pereira, with several European clubs, such as Paris Saint-Germain and Juventus, expressing interest in signing Pereira if he does not agree to the terms proposed by United.

Joel Burger, 24, proposed to his girlfriend Ashley King, also 23, leading to plans for a Burger King-themed wedding. The couple, who have known each other since kindergarten, intend to serve drinks in personalized Burger King cups for guests. They met as young children when a motivational speaker coined their names as "Burger King."

A secret police intelligence report from 1964 revealed that a hit band from the 1960s and the disgraced BBC presenter Jimmy Savile both frequented a notorious pedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London. Detective Superintendent David Grey, leading the investigation into Savile under Operation Yewtree, began looking into the brothel after it was referenced in another report in 2013. Despite the connection between the band and Savile, it remains unclear if they attended the brothel simultaneously, and no direct evidence linking them was found.

Sadie, a German Shepherd from Alberta, Canada, has been filmed using her nose to turn on an electric organ and then playing it with her paws, sitting on a piano stool. Despite appearing to struggle with the piece and even pausing to check if she made a mistake, the video of her performance has garnered over 12,000 views online. Sadie, who was adopted from an animal rescue shelter in 2009, enjoys learning new tricks, including playing the piano.

A phone thief named Ivan Balashov took a selfie in a Russian shop while trying to steal a smartphone he preferred, but was caught when police recognized him from the photo. After being stopped by shop security and attempting to flee, Balashov was later identified and arrested by the police who used the selfie as evidence. He received a three-month suspended sentence for his crime.

A documentary trailer for "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name" has been released, showcasing early footage of Amy Winehouse discussing her musical journey. The film aims to provide a comprehensive look at both the musical talent and the personal life of the late British singer, who struggled with addiction before her untimely death at 27. The documentary, featuring extensive unseen archive footage and previously unheard tracks, has been endorsed by Winehouse's family and is directed by the same team behind the award-winning "Senna" documentary.

The article highlights several TV shows recommended for viewers to watch, starting with "The Big Bang Theory," where veteran actresses Christine Baranski and Laurie Metcalf reprise their roles as the mothers of Sheldon and Leonard. It also mentions "Saturday Night Live" hosting Scarlett Johansson, "Mom" starring Allison Janney delivering another strong performance, and "Backstrom" with Rainn Wilson set to conclude its season. Additionally, it notes the season finales of "Blue Bloods" and "Younger," which has been picked up for a second season and features Sutton Foster and Hilary Duff.

Dame Maggie Smith's character, Violet, Countess of Grantham, from "Downton Abbey," may appear in a new American show called "The Gilded Age," which is set in 19th-century New York. The show, created by "Downton Abbey" producer Julian Fellowes, could feature other Downton characters like Robert, the Earl of Grantham, and his wife Cora, portrayed as younger versions of their Downton Abbey selves. NBC, the network behind "The Gilded Age," is optimistic about the project and hopes to bring it to air as early as September, pending finalization of plans.

Steven Gerrard, a 34-year-old Liverpool midfielder, is set to start in the FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley Stadium, likely marking his final appearance there before joining LA Galaxy. Manager Brendan Rodgers has chosen to include Gerrard in the lineup despite using him sparingly this season, with Gerrard looking to end his career with a trophy at Wembley. Rodgers praises Gerrard as a "special player" who has consistently delivered in big games.

A new Dr. Seuss book, "What Pet Should I Get?", has generated significant interest, leading to an increased first printing from 500,000 to 1 million copies to meet demand. This release marks the first new original Dr. Seuss book since 1990 and features the beloved characters from "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish." The manuscript was discovered in 2013 among the late Ted Geisel's belongings, adding to the excitement surrounding the publication.

Jessica Carey traveled over three hours to surprise her grandmother, Patty Lawing, with a tattoo of her from childhood. The tattoo, created by Jessica's husband, accurately depicted Patty as a young woman with long red hair and wearing a smart blouse and jacket. Patty's emotional reaction was captured on video, where she became overwhelmed and emotional upon seeing the portrait on Jessica's arm.

At 65 years old, Annegret Raunigk, a German primary school teacher, is expecting quadruplets through fertility treatment, making her the oldest known woman to carry such a pregnancy. This comes after she previously made headlines for giving birth to her youngest child at age 55. Her pregnancy, though high-risk due to her advanced age, is progressing well under close medical supervision.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, has announced plans to send an unmanned rover to the moon by 2018, aiming to develop soft-landing technologies that could be useful for future missions to the moon or even Mars. The mission, using a SLIM probe, is estimated to cost between $83.4 million and $125 million and will involve repurposing face recognition software for crater identification. This endeavor positions Japan as a contender in lunar exploration, potentially closing the gap with other Asian nations like China and India, which have already achieved significant milestones in space exploration.

Dengue fever has led to an outbreak in Brazil, affecting several top football clubs and forcing key players to miss matches. Notable cases include Corinthians striker Paolo Guerrero, who is hospitalized, and Palmeiras reserve goalkeeper Aranha, both of whom will miss crucial games. In response, clubs have taken measures such as using insect repellent and checking for mosquito breeding sites, while players practice with long clothing to avoid bites.

Manchester United striker James Wilson expressed his admiration for Wayne Rooney, Robin van Persie, and Radamel Falcao, stating that he would like to adopt Rooney's free-kicking ability, van Persie's movement, and Falcao's instincts in the penalty area. Wilson, who has scored two goals for the team this season, is using his time with the first team to learn from these experienced forwards. He particularly highlighted Rooney's consistent practice of free-kicks as something he wishes to emulate.

Archie Brown Jr., a 39-year-old van driver from Milwaukee, Wisconsin, struck and killed a 2-year-old child who ran in front of his vehicle. After the initial accident, an unknown individual approached the scene and shot both Brown and a 15-year-old boy, who later died from their injuries; the motive for the shooting remains unclear. The tragic incident left Brown's father, Archie Brown Sr., devastated, as he identified his son, who was a real estate entrepreneur and father of four, as the deceased driver.

A young boy from Memphis, Tennessee, with a surprisingly mature appearance, has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers by posting pictures of gang-related activities, including posing with guns and drugs, and making sexually explicit and confrontational comments. His posts have sparked criticism from the public, with some calling for his parents to take responsibility, while others suggest he needs help and an education. The boy has defended himself against the backlash, claiming his family has faced significant challenges and that his critics do not understand their situation.

Former Redgum frontman John Schumann criticized anti-Islam protesters for using his song "I Was Only 19" at Reclaim Australia rallies, which aimed to oppose sharia law and Islamization. Schumann, whose song is about compassion and tolerance, expressed disappointment in seeing his work co-opted by what he considers a confused "patriotic" movement. The rallies across the nation turned violent, with clashes between Reclaim Australia supporters and anti-racism groups leading to multiple arrests and minor injuries.

Emmanuel Adebayor, a forward for Tottenham Hotspur, has tweeted that he intends to stay with the club and fight for a place in the team, despite reports suggesting he may leave. The 31-year-old Togo international expressed his gratitude for playing in the Premier League, which he considers the best division in the world. However, Adebayor's form has significantly declined since joining Tottenham in 2011, with his last Premier League goal coming in October last year, and he has been overshadowed by the rising star Harry Kane.

Stuart Pearce advocates for giving Manchester City's manager, Manuel Pellegrini, more time to improve the team's performance despite their recent struggles. Pearce, who has experience with the club both as a player and manager, attributes the team's poor form partly to the declining influence of Yaya Toure. He also suggests that the club should consider refreshing their squad in the upcoming summer transfer window.

Steve Bruce remains optimistic about keeping Hull City in the Barclays Premier League despite a 2-0 defeat by Southampton and the team's current struggle to avoid relegation. Bruce attributes the team's difficulties to several long-term injuries to key players and expresses confidence that positive results in their remaining matches could secure their place in the league. Despite their recent setbacks, Bruce maintains that Hull City still has the potential to overcome their challenges and stay in the Premier League.

A full-scale terror alert was triggered in Reading when a passer-by reported seeing a barge on the Thames with a fake missile launcher and a dummy in a balaclava nearby. Thames Valley Police and an Army bomb disposal team were called to the scene but found the weapon to be purely ornamental. Local residents expressed disappointment and concern over the prank, deeming it reckless and inappropriate given the recent terrorist threats.

Tiger Woods suffered an unusual injury during his play at the Masters when his club hit a tree root, causing him pain and forcing him to drop his club. Despite the setback, Woods managed to finish the tournament at 5-under-par, marking his best performance in over a year. He attributed the injury to a popped wrist ligament that he managed to pop back in place, allowing him to continue playing.

Iker Casillas asserts he will remain at Real Madrid and compete for the starting goalkeeper position despite potential competition from Manchester United's David de Gea. Casillas, who has been with Real Madrid since 1996, emphasizes his commitment to fulfilling his contract and contributing to the team’s goal of retaining the Champions League title. He also expresses optimism about the upcoming semi-finals, viewing the match-ups against strong European teams as highly competitive and exciting.

Embarrassing footage has surfaced showing a S300 missile launch in Russia that went spectacularly wrong, barely leaving the launchpad before falling back to the ground, causing a small explosion and leaving a large plume of smoke. This incident comes amid increased defense spending under President Putin, who has boosted the budget by 33% to £54 billion. The embarrassing video follows another recent failed rocket launch near Donetsk, Ukraine, which resulted in the deaths of six Russian missile technicians and was initially kept secret by officials.

Lancashire County Cricket Club has signed Australian all-rounder James Faulkner as their overseas player for the majority of the summer, replacing Peter Siddle. Faulkner, who recently won the World Cup for Australia, will join the team after completing his Indian Premier League commitments. Head coach Ashley Giles expresses excitement about Faulkner's addition, praising his world-class status and potential benefits to the team's performance.

In 1996, Mary Kay Letourneau, a 34-year-old teacher, had an affair with her 13-year-old student, leading to her imprisonment for over seven years. Since her release in 2005, she has remarried Vili Fualaau and celebrated their 10th wedding anniversary, now parenting two teenage daughters together. The upcoming "20/20" interview will delve into how they maintain their relationship despite significant age differences and personal challenges, including Letourneau's plans to teach again and efforts to have her sex offender status lifted.

Jamie Carragher traveled to Spain during the international break to support his son James, who was playing for the Liverpool U12s in the Mediterranean International Cup in Girona. Carragher shared his experience through an Instagram post of the opening ceremony and provided commentary for local television. The Liverpool team, in their debut match, drew 1-1 against a local Catalan side, CE Mercantil, as part of the tournament that has featured notable players like Philippe Coutinho and Lionel Messi in previous years.

Seattle-based filmmaker Gabriel Ng spent three months in Thailand, capturing breathtaking views of the country's coastlines, religious sites, and daily life through drone footage, resulting in a six-minute video that showcases the beauty of destinations like Ko Samui. The video, featuring stunning shots of beaches, waterfalls, and temples, has garnered praise for its high-definition quality and has been compared to professional productions despite being made with relatively affordable drone technology. Gabriel Ng, who owns a video production company, has previously used similar methods to capture aerial footage for various clients, including weddings and famous landmarks.

Peter Moores stated that he is open to working with Michael Vaughan if he becomes England's new director of cricket, emphasizing that it is not a personal issue but rather about building a strong team. Moores expressed doubt about whether the team needs another voice in the dressing room, depending on how the new role is defined. Despite the recent departures and restructuring within the England cricket team, Moores remains focused on his coaching duties and is optimistic about the emerging talent, maintaining that his position and responsibilities will remain unchanged.

Nottingham Forest plans to pursue a transfer for Blackburn's striker Jordan Rhodes, who is valued at £10 million, with Forest manager Dougie Freedman hoping a direct cash offer will succeed where previous attempts failed. Blackburn initially rejected Forest's March bid for Rhodes, despite interest from several other clubs. Meanwhile, Blackburn's Gary Bowyer anticipates further interest in striker Rudy Gestede, who recently scored 19 goals including one against Forest, with several clubs showing interest in the French-born player.

In a heartwarming scene captured in a North Carolina home, a trio of dogs—Sky the Husky, Sadie and Marshall the Springer Spaniels—put on a unique musical performance for their owner. Starting with Sadie's barking and followed by Sky's melodious howl, the dogs harmonize, with Sky playfully interacting with Sadie and the third Springer Spaniel becoming excited. The video ends as the owner asks for quiet, leaving the dogs looking surprised and slightly disappointed.

The "French Spiderman," Alain Robert, climbed the 1,007-foot Cayan Tower in Dubai without a safety harness, using only sticky tape and chalk for assistance, taking about an hour and a half to reach the top. Known for his daring climbs, Robert has previously faced legal troubles and injuries but has also complied with safety regulations in other climbs, such as his 2011 ascent of the Burj Khalifa. His latest climb drew hundreds of spectators and was documented on video.

An experimental cancer drug previously abandoned due to poor results has shown promise in reversing the effects of Alzheimer's disease when tested on mice. The drug, AZDO5030, works by blocking a process that damages nerve connections in the brain responsible for memory storage. Researchers at Yale University have now initiated human trials to assess its effectiveness in Alzheimer's patients, with initial results indicating potential for restoring memory and reducing inflammation.

The article discusses the buildup of anticipation for the release of "Avengers: Age of Ultron" by revealing the appearance of the Vision, an android character played by Paul Bettany. It also mentions the upcoming release of the Netflix series "Daredevil" and the announcement of a new character, Angel, for the upcoming "X-Men: Apocalypse." Additionally, it highlights the reveal of Jamie Bell's character, The Thing, in the rebooted "Fantastic Four" movie, addressing fan speculation about his appearance.

Veteran referee Kenny Bayless will officiate the highly anticipated boxing match between Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao, having previously worked with both fighters in numerous bouts. Despite being widely regarded as one of the best referees in the world, some, like former opponent Oscar De La Hoya, believe Bayless's involvement gives Mayweather an advantage due to past interactions where Bayless frequently broke up clinches. The appointment has sparked debate among boxing enthusiasts regarding its potential impact on the outcome of the match.

Harry Kane's participation in the upcoming Under-21 European Championship is uncertain due to Tottenham Hotspur's scheduled post-season friendly in Malaysia. Manager Mauricio Pochettino is concerned about potential burnout for the 21-year-old striker, while the Football Association is in discussions with Tottenham about Kane's availability for the tournament. Kane is expected to accompany the team to Malaysia for friendly matches, but may miss the Under-21 European Championship to ensure adequate rest before the start of the new season.

A measles outbreak affecting over 130 people in California due to a B3 strain has been declared over by the California Department of Public Health after 42 days without new cases. The majority of those affected (70%) were found to be unvaccinated, highlighting the importance of vaccination. The outbreak originated from visitors to two Disney theme parks in December, and while it was contained, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have identified 19 different strains of measles since 1990.

In San Miguel de Tucuman, Argentina, police are searching for a family of six caught on camera riding on a single motorbike, with two adults and four children aboard, including young children sitting in front without helmets. This incident follows a similar case in Junin where a family of seven was photographed on the same motorbike, both drawing strong condemnation from the public and authorities. Both families were reportedly without helmets and their behavior considered extremely dangerous.

Andrea McVeigh, a 44-year-old social media manager, was seriously injured when she was struck by a cyclist while walking on the pavement in Bermondsey, London. The cyclist fled the scene, prompting the involvement of the victim's husband and passersby, and leaving McVeigh with significant facial injuries that have left her scarred for life. The Metropolitan Police have released CCTV footage of the cyclist and are seeking the public's assistance in identifying and apprehending the perpetrator.

A few days after Hillary Clinton announced her candidacy for the presidency, her father's headstone, located in the Washburn Street Cemetery in Scranton, Pennsylvania, was found tipped over. The grave tendsman, Paul McGloin, noticed the headstone had fallen shortly after driving past it on Monday morning. While police suspect vandalism, they are also considering whether weather could have caused the incident.

A California woman, Beatriz Paez, was recorded by another woman as she was filming police activity with her cell phone. When Paez refused to stop, a U.S. marshal physically took the phone, smashed it with his foot, and kicked it away, leaving Paez feeling unsafe and terrified. Paez has since filed a complaint and is considering legal action against the marshal's actions, which she considers illegal as she was not interfering with any investigation or arrest.

Max, a 18.5-inch-tall corgi-Siberian husky cross, has become a favorite at the Dogs Trust in Basildon, Essex, where he was taken in as a stray. Known for his gentle, intelligent, and big-hearted nature, Max exemplifies the saying "good things come in small packages." His popularity is partly attributed to the rising trend of owning wolf-like breeds, driven by fans of shows like Game of Thrones, though this trend often leads to the abandonment of such dogs due to inadequate preparation for their specific needs.

Chilean pickpockets have emerged as the most effective thieves in central London, targeting wealthy tourists in areas such as the West End. According to undercover police reports, these gangs, often consisting of three to six individuals, operate with high precision, blending into groups that appear harmless to avoid detection, and have been known to carry large sums of money and valuable items. The Metropolitan Police, working to reduce theft, note that while pickpocketing remains a significant issue, there has been a notable 50% decrease in theft cases over the past year.

In a severe car accident near Southam, Warwickshire, a young driver's vehicle crashed into a wall, flipped over, and left him trapped underneath. Despite suffering head, chest, and leg injuries, the man survived the crash and remained conscious throughout the rescue operation, which took 25 minutes. Emergency services, including firefighters and the air ambulance, worked together to free him from the wreckage.

In a Suffolk village, a gang of fly-tippers dumped an astonishing 40 tonnes of industrial waste along the roadside, described by a police officer as the worst case he had seen in nearly 30 years. The materials included items from the carpet and veterinary industries and were reportedly transported using three tractors and trailers. This incident, which occurred late Thursday evening, has prompted local authorities and environmental agencies to launch efforts to both clean up the mess and catch the responsible parties.

A man, believed to be mentally disturbed, attempted to enter a restricted area at Pearson International Airport in Toronto and refused to comply with security protocols, leading to his tasering by police. The incident was captured on video, showing the man mumble and stare ahead as he was Tasered, causing him to fall to the ground after several seconds of visible trembling. Subsequently, the man was transferred to a hospital under Canada's Mental Health Act and may face no criminal charges.

Serbia's President Tomislav Nikolic's government jet had to turn back to Belgrade after the co-pilot accidentally spilled coffee on the instrument panel, causing the plane to begin tumbling through the air. The incident, which left advisers "thrown around the cabin," was initially blamed on engine failure but was later confirmed to be due to the co-pilot activating the emergency slats by mistake while trying to clean the spill. As a result, the president had to cancel his planned meeting with Pope Francis in the Vatican, and the co-pilot had his license suspended.

In South Africa, over 300 suspects have been arrested in connection with violent attacks against foreigners, which have led to the displacement of thousands seeking refuge in temporary shelters. The government condemned the attacks and credited law enforcement for preventing further casualties, while also reminding citizens of the country's history of accepting refugees. Despite the violence, there has been an outpouring of support from ordinary South Africans and organizations like the Gift of the Givers, which is offering assistance to those affected.

A skier named Zach Birnie captured a harrowing experience of being caught in an avalanche while skiing off-piste in Revelstoke, Canada. Despite the terrifying ordeal, Birnie managed to escape and resurface, though he later noted he had injured his shoulder and lost one ski pole. An expert from the WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research advised that if caught in a similar situation, one should try to escape the avalanche area, release ski bindings if possible, pull knees to the chest, and protect the face.

On the hottest day of the year, two men in their 20s, who stripped off their tops, attempted to rob an Esso petrol station in Caterham, Surrey. The men entered the manager's office to search for cash but were interrupted by a staff member and fled without taking any money. Surrey Police released CCTV footage of the suspects and are asking the public for help in identifying them.

The Lada Niva 4x4, starting at £13,395 on the road, is gaining popularity as an alternative to the now-defunct Land Rover Defender, thanks to its robust design and affordable price. Despite being a Russian brand that was once the subject of ridicule, the Niva has won fans worldwide due to its durability and distinctive appearance, even available in a compact van format for £10,590. However, while the Niva lacks luxury features, its simple design means it's easy to maintain, as evidenced by its use by then-Russian President Vladimir Putin, who reportedly fitted his Niva with a German engine.

AIDS Healthcare Foundation, the largest provider of HIV and AIDS medical care in the U.S., is accused of a $20 million scam involving kickbacks for patient referrals to boost funding from Medicare and Medicaid across 12 states. Three former managers have filed a lawsuit alleging the company paid employees and patients $100 bonuses for referring patients with positive test results, starting in 2010 from the California headquarters and spreading to other locations. The foundation denies wrongdoing and maintains its approach to identifying and treating HIV is critical for public health.

Liz, a bearded dragon owned by Shannen Hussein, has been caught on video nodding her head in response to being asked if she is hungry, demonstrating an apparent understanding of human speech. Following this interaction, Liz is rewarded with a superworm treat, which she enjoys greatly. Additionally, Shannen's pet lamb, Winter, has also gained internet fame through various Vine videos showcasing its playful antics around the home and with other pets.

Travis Hatfield, an aspiring country singer from West Virginia, gained viral attention after posting a video of him singing to his uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome. The heartfelt performance of "He Stopped Loving Her Today" has garnered over 410,000 views and showcases the strong bond between the two. Inspired by his uncle's love for music, Travis dreams of pursuing a career in country music and plans to audition for The Voice and release his own CD.

Nik Wallenda, the daredevil from the 'Flying Wallenda' family, plans to walk untethered on a 400-foot observation wheel in Orlando, Florida, on April 29. The Orlando Eye, an attraction that will open to the public on May 4, features enclosed capsules offering views of central Florida. This stunt, while not the full circumference of the wheel, is considered particularly challenging due to the wheel's size and its movement during the performance.

Medhi Benatia, a central defender for Bayern Munich, is likely to miss both legs of the team's upcoming Champions League quarter-final against Porto due to a muscle injury that may keep him out for two to four weeks. This adds to Bayern Munich's already lengthy injury list, which includes key players like Bastian Schweinsteiger, David Alaba, Javi Martinez, and Tom Starke. Despite the injuries, Bayern Munich remains competitive in multiple competitions, including the Bundesliga where they lead by ten points and still have aspirations in the Champions League.

Bayern Munich defeated Porto 6-1 in the Champions League quarter-final second leg, advancing to the semi-finals and demonstrating their dominance under coach Pep Guardiola. This victory adds to their already impressive season, with a total of 115 goals scored across all competitions, including the Bundesliga, German Cup, and Champions League. At their current pace, they could potentially score up to 141 goals by the end of the season, putting immense pressure on other European teams to match their extraordinary form.

Fernando Torres credits Diego Simeone as the key figure behind Atletico Madrid's recent success, attributing their performances to Simeone's understanding of the team's strengths and weaknesses. Despite not having the resources of top teams like Real Madrid and Barcelona, Atletico Madrid has exceeded expectations under Simeone's leadership and has not lost to their rivals in six matches since the 2014 Champions League final. Torres, who has scored four goals since returning to Atletico, emphasizes that the team must play at their limit without the luxury of making up for dropped points.

Two bodies have been found among the wreckage of a light aircraft that crashed near Loch Etive in Argyll, Scotland. The plane was last known to be traveling from central Scotland to Tiree Island when it lost contact with ground control, prompting a search involving lifeboats, helicopters, and police. The incident is under investigation, and authorities are seeking any information that could help clarify the circumstances surrounding the crash.

A bus shatters the windscreen of a Boeing 777 passenger jet at Tashkent airport in Uzbekistan, causing significant damage but no apparent injuries. This incident, along with recent collisions involving Ryanair and British Airways, highlights the increasing frequency of such accidents at major airports globally, often resulting in delays and disruptions for passengers. These events underscore the importance of improved safety measures and better coordination among ground staff and pilots.

An off-duty Secret Service agent, Arthur Baldwin, was arrested in Washington D.C. on felony charges of attempted burglary and destruction of property after allegedly breaking into a house at midnight. The agency revoked Baldwin's security clearance and placed him on leave pending the outcome of the investigation. This incident follows other recent controversies within the Secret Service, including a supervisor being put on leave for alleged misconduct and an incident where high-ranking officials drove into a restricted area of the White House while intoxicated.

Israel is developing a unique tunnelling detection system, designed to accurately identify underground activity without false alarms, following extensive consideration of over 700 proposals. The system, developed by Elbit Systems in collaboration with the Israeli Ministry of Defense, is expected to cost approximately £2.3 million per mile to install and will be deployed along the Gaza-Israel border. Initial tests have been successful, with further results expected soon.

A primary school in south London has banned all drinks except water during the school day to promote long-term pupil health, but this decision has sparked a parental backlash. Parents argue that the ban is too strict and that children should have the freedom to choose their own beverages, especially since many do not enjoy plain water. Despite the controversy, the school defends the policy as a means to protect students' health, aligning with similar measures taken at other schools.

Paul Smith will face undefeated boxer Andre Ward in a high-stakes boxing match on June 20 in Oakland, California. This fight represents a significant opportunity for Smith, who previously lost attempts to win the WBO title, as it comes after Ward's last bout in November 2013, potentially introducing some "ring rust" to the equation. Both fighters expressed their excitement and determination for the upcoming clash, with Ward emphasizing the need to perform at his best to overcome the challenging opponent.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel and her husband, Joachim Sauer, were spotted on their annual Easter holiday on the island of Ischia in Italy, where they typically stay at the five-star Miramare Spa Hotel. Despite the lack of sunshine in comparison to Britain, where temperatures reached up to 21C, Mrs. Merkel focused on staying healthy, hiring a private Pilates instructor and sticking to vegetarian meals. Her husband, a chemistry professor, largely kept to the background, as he often does during their trips.

Ander Herrera, a Manchester United midfielder, has scored several goals without looking at the ball or the goal, including a brace against Aston Villa where his eyes appeared to be shut during both goals. This unusual goal-scoring habit has raised questions about his vision, despite him being signed for their excellent kicking technique and creativity. Manager Louis van Gaal noted that Herrera needs to improve his ball control before shooting, suggesting this might be an area for development.

A 23-month-old girl tragically died after her father accidentally struck her with a pickup truck in the driveway of their home in North Las Vegas. The father and other family members were unaware that the toddler had wandered outside. The incident was ruled an accident, and no charges were filed.

The University of Connecticut baseball team has welcomed 5-year-old Grayson Hand, a child battling leukemia, as its newest member with the assistance of Team IMPACT. Grayson's involvement includes having his own locker and attending team practices and games, while his sister Sophie has been named an honorary cheerleader. This partnership symbolizes the broader support network Grayson and his family have received during his battle with cancer.

A passenger on a London Midland train discovered excrement in a newspaper on the floor, causing severe delays and forcing the train to terminate early for cleaning. London Midland has vowed to provide CCTV footage of the suspect to the police for investigation. The incident, which occurred on the Cross City line, led to hours of disruption for commuters and highlights the ongoing issue of public transportation hygiene.

James Rodriguez, the Colombian midfielder who transferred to Real Madrid for £60 million last summer, has quickly become a fan favorite and a key player for the team, as reported by Spanish newspaper Marca. His presence in the lineup has significantly boosted Real Madrid's winning percentage to 80%, compared to 58% without him. Meanwhile, in Italy, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports that former Manchester City manager Roberto Mancini plans to make significant summer signings, aiming to strengthen Inter Milan with a potential eight new players from a list of 21 candidates.

A Florida man named Kenneth Crowder, who was believed to be under the influence of Flakka, a powerful and dangerous synthetic drug, attacked a police officer after being tased twice, during which he claimed he was God and attempted to stab the officer with a police badge. Crowder was arrested and charged with battery on a law-enforcement officer, resisting with violence, and assault with a deadly weapon on a law-enforcement officer. Flakka, similar in effects to a mix of crack cocaine and methamphetamine, has become increasingly prevalent in Florida, with over 670 incidents reported in 2014 alone.

A Russian Premier League match between Arsenal Tula and Torpedo Moscow was suspended for seven minutes on Sunday due to fighting between rival fans, with Torpedo supporters breaking down barriers and throwing seats at law enforcement officers. The incident led to harsh criticism of Torpedo, with their executive director expecting severe punishment, as this is not the first time the club has faced such issues. Torpedo has already been penalized three times this season for fan-related misconduct, including a recent incident where fans abused a player.

High school girls in Huizhou, China, are undergoing military-style dagger drill training under the guidance of a former special forces soldier, aimed at teaching them self-defense techniques. The training, conducted by Inspector Tan, involves the use of non-harmful, retractable-blade knives and includes eight defensive movements; the girls also practice using everyday objects like chopsticks for defense. All female students at the school receive such training, emphasizing the importance of recognizing dangerous situations and defending oneself.

AP McCoy, the champion jockey since 1997, is urging supporters to root for his horse, Shutthefrontdoor, in the Grand National to secure a fairytale victory that would end his career on a high note. Despite the unpredictability of the race, McCoy remains optimistic and believes that his dreams could come true, though he acknowledges the slim chances. McCoy plans to retire immediately if his horse wins, aiming to end his record-breaking career with a triumph in the £1 million race.

John Isner advanced to the Miami Open semifinals with a straight-sets victory over Kei Nishikori, becoming the first American male to reach the semifinals in Miami since 2011. In contrast, Andy Murray will face Tomas Berdych in the other semifinal, with an interesting dynamic as both were coached by former teammates who now work for Berdych. The tennis atmosphere between Isner and Nishikori remained cordial, while Murray and Berdych's match promises to be charged with tension due to their history and past conflicts.

Former German football legend Franz Beckenbauer criticized Bayern Munich's performance in their Champions League loss to Porto, comparing it to players taking "sleeping pills." He specifically targeted defender Dante, saying his performance was akin to wearing "ski boots." Despite his harsh words, Beckenbauer still maintained hope for Bayern Munich's chances in the competition, provided they improve significantly.

A 21-year-old man named Arnold Quintero from San Antonio, Texas, has been arrested for allegedly imprisoning, beating, sexually assaulting, and burning a 13-year-old girl. The girl reported being held in a "trap house" and subjected to physical violence, forced undressing, and sexual assault by Quintero, who also took photos during the incident. Quintero faces multiple charges including aggravated sexual assault of a child and possession with intent to deliver, among others.

In Week 12 of the Betway Premier League, Michael van Gerwen and Gary Anderson experienced contrasting results, each winning and losing a game. Van Gerwen dominated with a 7-0 win over James Wade but later lost to Anderson. Anderson, after an initial loss to Stephen Bunting, secured a 7-5 victory over Van Gerwen with a strong average score.

Jay Rutland, the husband of billionaire heiress Tamara Ecclestone, earns only £65 per week from his consulting firm, which brought in just £3,378 over the past year. Despite his low income from his business, Rutland and his wife live in a £45 million house and have access to expensive luxuries, including a Ferrari, Bentley, and Range Rover. The couple's financial disparity highlights the vast wealth difference between Rutland, who was previously a stockbroker but is now struggling financially, and his wealthy family.

Jia Binhui, a 25-year-old man from southwest China, is using an unconventional method of lying over hot coals daily in the hope of killing off his leukemia cells, as he cannot afford traditional medical treatment. This homemade "barbecue" setup, built in his garden, is based on the belief that temperatures exceeding 42 degrees Celsius can eliminate cancer cells. Despite his desperate attempt, Jia has already undergone a bone marrow transplant, funded by well-wishers, and continues to marry his long-term girlfriend while refusing to surrender to the disease.

Leroy Fer, a Dutch midfielder for Queens Park Rangers, is set to return to the squad after recovering from a knee injury, potentially boosting the team's chances in their relegation battle. Manager Chris Ramsey hopes Fer will be available for the upcoming match against West Ham, despite the player not yet being fully fit. Ramsey acknowledges the risk but sees it as necessary to give Fer a chance to prove himself and contribute to the team's efforts to avoid relegation.

In the final kilometre of the Scheldeprijs race, Team Sky teammates Sir Bradley Wiggins and Geraint Thomas escaped a major crash that involved around 50 riders, including their teammate Elia Viviani, who sustained injuries and required x-rays. The crash marred what had been a successful day for Team Sky, with Wiggins preparing for the upcoming Paris-Roubaix on Sunday. Alexander Kristoff emerged as the winner after a reduced sprint finish following the incident.

Before their FA Cup semi-final match against Liverpool, Aston Villa's players received encouraging messages from fans displayed in their dressing room at Wembley Stadium. Teenage star Jack Grealish tweeted one such message, which read, "You have to put up with the rain to see the rainbow! Three seasons of rain boys, time to find the end of that rainbow and prove we're the pride of the Midlands!" Additionally, goalkeeper Brad Guzan shared that he had received a message telling the team to "fight like Lions."

A 12-year-old boy named Hanghang in central China suffered severe injuries when his old mobile phone exploded while charging, exposing parts of his jawbone and embedding fragments in his arms and legs. Doctors at Ping Mei Group Hospital are treating him and expect multiple surgeries to repair the damage. Experts suggest improper charging is the most common cause of such explosions, along with damaged batteries and illegal modifications, emphasizing the importance of proper charging practices to prevent similar incidents.

Mike Rowe, known for his work on "Dirty Jobs," highlights Chad Pregracke, the founder of Living Lands & Waters, who has dedicated over 20 years to cleaning U.S. waterways and collecting 8.4 million pounds of trash with the help of over 87,000 volunteers. Pregracke was honored as the 2013 CNN Hero of the Year and uses a solar-powered, repurposed barge for extended cleanup missions. He aims to remove an additional 500,000 pounds of trash in 2015 and encourages others to join in the effort through their website.

The ancient Tuscan town of Balestrino, dating back to the 11th century, became uninhabited due to seismic instability from multiple earthquakes, including one measuring 6.7 on the Richter scale in 1887. Now considered the most famous abandoned location in Italy, the town, once home to 800 inhabitants, is shrouded in mystery and folklore suggesting it is haunted. Drone footage captures the eerie beauty of the deserted town, featuring a grand castle and decaying buildings overgrown with vegetation.

At an emotional event in Anaheim, California, the cast and director of "Star Wars: Episode VII -- The Force Awakens" presented a trailer for the new film, eliciting gasps, cheers, and applause from the audience. The event featured the introduction of new characters, sets, and technology, including the BB8 droid, and revealed that the movie would be shot on actual sets rather than relying heavily on CGI. The film, directed by J.J. Abrams, is set to release on December 18, with key elements of the plot including the return of Han Solo, hints of Luke and Leia, and a new shooting location called Jakku.

Former Toronto Mayor Rob Ford announced plans to undergo surgery in May to remove a cancerous tumor in his abdomen, which has been reduced in size through chemotherapy and radiation. Ford, who previously faced political challenges including a drug scandal, hopes to return to work as a city councilor in September. Despite the significant health setback, Ford expressed gratitude for the support he received and remained optimistic about his prognosis.

At the University of Cape Town, a decades-old statue of Cecil Rhodes, a British colonialist, was removed after weeks of student protests under the hashtag #RhodesMustFall, reflecting students' desire to confront and address the legacy of racism and colonialism. However, the decision sparked controversy as some Afrikaner groups saw the removal as an attempt to erase history rather than a step towards a more inclusive narrative. The event highlighted ongoing debates about how to reckon with the past and promote a more equitable future in South Africa.

Michael Phelps won the 100 meters butterfly event at the Arena Pro Swim Series in Arizona, marking his return to competitive swimming after a six-month suspension due to a drink-driving conviction. The 18-time Olympic gold medalist expressed joy at being back in competition, despite missing the upcoming World Championships. Phelps, who aims to compete in the 2016 Olympics in Rio, indicated that he will not participate in the World Championships in Kazan, Russia, following discussions with USA Swimming.

A woman was found hanging from a fire escape in Crown Heights, New York, with her body left dangling for over an hour. Neighbors were traumatized by the discovery, with one witness initially believing it was a Halloween prank. The victim, whose identity remains undisclosed, had a history of mental health issues and was described by locals as a "very social, nice girl" who couldn't come out of a "dark spot."

Lyon reclaimed the top spot in Ligue 1 with a 2-2 draw against Saint-Etienne in a thrilling Rhone derby, despite being down to 10 men for part of the match. Meanwhile, Lille maintained their pursuit of a top-four finish by defeating Bordeaux 2-0, keeping within four points of fourth place. Additionally, Montpellier secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Caen thanks to an early header from Brazilian defender Hilton, helping them move up to seventh place in the standings.

Arsenal manager Arsène Wenger admitted he did not initially expect key players Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin to be contributing so significantly to the team's late push for the Premier League title. Bellerin, who had only recently returned from a loan spell at Watford, scored a crucial goal against Liverpool, while Coquelin has become a regular first-team fixture despite a previous loan to Charlton. Wenger praised both players for their performances, acknowledging that their contributions have been unexpected yet invaluable.

Fox is developing a two-hour remake of the cult classic "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" for television, set to be directed, executive-produced, and choreographed by Kenneth Ortega. Scheduled to celebrate the film's 40th anniversary, the project, tentatively titled "The Rocky Horror Picture Show Event," will be filmed in advance and aims to recreate the show's enduring popularity through a new adaptation. This follows previous attempts to bring the musical to the small screen, including a 2002 Fox plan that was ultimately abandoned.

Roma FC has been ordered to close part of their stadium for their next home game due to offensive banners displayed by their supporters during a recent match against Napoli. These banners, which insulted the mother of a Napoli fan who died in violent clashes following a previous match, were deemed provocative by a Serie A disciplinary tribunal. In response, the club's president has condemned the behavior, emphasizing the need for respect and unity in light of such tragic events.

Ellen White scored a stunning goal against her former club, Arsenal, in the Women's Super League, executing a perfect set-piece from training in the 26th minute. The goal came after confusion in the Arsenal defense following a free kick awarded to Notts County. Despite the memorable score, White also missed a penalty opportunity and later regretted the team's inability to capitalize on their chances, as Arsenal eventually equalized to salvage a draw.

Arsene Wenger acknowledges that his decision to let Eden Hazard join Chelsea in 2012 for £32 million was a significant financial one, as talks for his transfer nearly reached an agreement in his house. Despite this, Wenger maintains he has no regrets, attributing the inability to sign Hazard to financial constraints and the competitive nature of the transfer market. Wenger now sees Hazard as a top contender for the Player of the Year award, praising his improved performance and maturity, while also believing that his own forward, Alexis Sanchez, could also be in contention.

Stephen Akers-Belcher, the Mayor of Hartlepool, was dismissed from his position as a care manager with Newcastle City Council after claiming he needed time off for a funeral but was found to have visited HMS Warrior instead. The council denied he was dismissed for whistleblowing and stated that his allegations about the protection of vulnerable adults were thoroughly investigated without any further action being taken. The dismissal was due to gross misconduct, as Akers-Belcher could not provide evidence of attending a funeral and failed to provide relevant information to the employment tribunal.

Dr. John Parker, a humanitarian doctor who had been working in an Ebola treatment clinic in Sierra Leone, tested negative for the Ebola virus after showing symptoms of an influenza-like illness upon returning to Australia. He was taken to Westmead Hospital in Sydney for evaluation, and NSW Health confirmed that no further testing for Ebola was necessary. Dr. Parker had followed protocol and notified authorities as a precaution after noticing a slight increase in his temperature upon returning from Sierra Leone.

A schoolboy named Frankie Franz, inspired by Barcelona's Martin Montoya, successfully replicated a 27-yard goal into a basketball hoop, surprising both his teammates and family. After watching Montoya perform the trick shot, Frankie attempted the feat himself in his garden and managed to score on his first try, much to his amazement and his mother's delight. The young center midfielder, who aspires to play for top clubs like Real Madrid or Barcelona, demonstrated remarkable skill by scoring again shortly after, leaving everyone impressed.

The Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014 short-list features stunning images capturing the global appeal of cricket, from professional athletes like Dwayne Bravo making spectacular catches to amateur players in unique settings such as on a rubbish tip in Bangladesh or on the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro. Notably, the winning photograph by Matthew Lewis showcases Bravo's extraordinary full-length catch during the ICC World Twenty20. The collection also includes poignant moments such as England's Stuart Broad breaking his nose from a stray ball and the aftermath of Australian batsman Phillip Hughes being fatally struck by a cricket ball.

In a custody dispute, a New Jersey judge dismissed a father's claim that his ex-wife abused her parental discretion by taking their 11-year-old daughter to see Pink's concert, ruling that the performances were not sexually inappropriate for a preteen. The judge, after considering the mother's reasons and speaking with the child, found no evidence of bad parenting and stated that the girl had a positive experience. The judge also noted that Pink's work, while sometimes suggestive, could be considered age-appropriate for young teenagers.

Salcombe, a coastal town in Devon, has surpassed London as the most expensive place in the UK to buy property, with the average property costing £671,759. This surge in property values has also driven up the cost of waterfront properties to over £2 million, surpassing some of London's priciest areas such as Notting Hill and Regent's Park. As a result, Salcombe, known as "Chelsea-on-Sea," continues to attract wealthy residents and tourists seeking a luxurious yet relatively affordable coastal lifestyle.

Celtic Football Club has criticized the Scottish Football Association (SFA) over the ticket prices for their upcoming Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness Caledonian Thistle at Hampden Park. Celtic argued that the North Stand tickets should be cheaper to align with other sections of the stadium, particularly given the high concentration of Celtic supporters. The SFA defended its decision, stating that all four participating clubs were consulted on the pricing, which has remained unchanged for four years, and that revenues from the matches are distributed evenly among the teams.

A 16-year-old student named Rebecca Rice was allowed to bring her pet Labrador, Holly, into a GCSE French oral exam to help calm her nerves, as none of the usual calming methods had worked for her. Rebecca's teacher, Lorette Esteve, suggested the idea after noticing that nothing else was helping Rebecca during the exam preparation. During the five-minute test, Holly sat beside Rebecca, and this arrangement proved effective in reducing Rebecca's anxiety.

Anders Lindegaard, a Manchester United goalkeeper who has struggled for playing time, shared a sunny day out with his wife Misse Beqiri on Instagram, reminding fans of their happy relationship. Lindegaard, a Danish international, has been with the stunning Swedish model and mother of his son since 2012, though his career at Manchester United has seen limited success. Off the pitch, however, Lindegaard and Beqiri's relationship appears to thrive, with Beqiri frequently sharing her own glamorous images on social media.

Spanish goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes took advantage of the sunny weather by visiting a theme park, a moment of relaxation for Manchester United just days after their impressive victory over Manchester City. This comes as a turnaround for the team under Louis van Gaal, who have recently secured a top-four position in the Premier League, despite earlier struggles. However, uncertainty looms as both players' contracts may not extend beyond the current season, making their future with the team uncertain.

A 75-year-old piano teacher, John Goodwin, shot himself outside a New Hampshire courthouse while awaiting a jury's verdict on six charges of aggravated felonious sexual assault. The former student, now 24, testified that he did not report the alleged assaults earlier due to embarrassment, and Goodwin's defense argued that while the teacher was "touchy-feely," he did not commit a crime. Goodwin was taken to the hospital with life-threatening injuries, but details of his condition were not immediately disclosed.

Amazon removed a controversial mobile game called "Rescue the Anorexia Girl," which encouraged players to throw food at a cartoon anorexic girl to prevent her from losing weight, from its platform after receiving numerous complaints. Scientists are working to digitally recreate the cognitive abilities of the honeybee to develop a robot that mimics its thinking, sensing, and acting capabilities. This project, known as the Green Brain Project, involves researchers from the Universities of Sheffield and Sussex and aims to create drones that can perform tasks such as pollinating crops and assisting in search and rescue missions. A newlywed couple from Air Malta recently took a romantic flight over the Mediterranean, with their passenger jet flying in the shape of two giant hearts shortly after takeoff. This unusual flight path was to celebrate the marriage of one of the pilots to a cabin crew member, with the flight also carrying the couple's family, friends, and colleagues on a short sight-seeing tour. At Kristiansand Zoo in Norway, a tragic incident occurred on Easter Monday where Melvin, a five-year-old giraffe, died after being gored by an eland antelope while his head was stuck in the enclosure's fence. The attack, which took place in front of around 30 witnesses including children, was unprovoked, and despite efforts by veterinarians, the giraffe could not be saved. North Korea accused Mexico of illegally detaining one of its cargo ships, the Mu Du Bong, which had run aground off Mexico's coast in July. Hazel, an English Bulldog puppy, demonstrates her playful and enthusiastic nature in a video where she tries to navigate a washing basket, causing it to tip over multiple times. Catholic bishops in the United States have criticized the BBC drama "Wolf Hall," describing it as a "prejudice-laden presentation of the past" due to its allegedly anti-Catholic portrayal of historical figures. A Fenerbahce team bus returning from an away match was attacked near Trabzon, Turkey, with gunfire, injuring the bus driver but leaving no other players or staff hurt. TV presenter Lisa Oldfield decided to undergo liposuction after her son's unflattering sketch of her highlighted her dissatisfaction with her appearance, particularly how it affected her relationship with her children. Motivated by the desire to spend more quality time with her young sons and improve her self-image, Oldfield now aims to maintain her new figure without the need for regular gym sessions.

Sarah and Mark Brennan, a couple from south Wales, endured ten miscarriages over ten years before finally giving birth to their daughter, Eryn, via a premature C-section at 33 weeks. Sarah encourages others struggling with infertility to persevere, emphasizing that hope can lead to joy.

To celebrate the 10th anniversary of the Football League Awards, a team of standout players from below England's top tier over the past decade has been assembled, featuring a mix of current Premier League stars and former lower-tier standouts. Irish boxer Andy Lee, defending his WBO middleweight title, expresses confidence in his improved skills and is set to face former champion Peter Quillin in a fight at the Barclays Centre.
